summary: Full-extraction pass over the Saint Lucia CBI legislation (Act 2015 and amendment Act 2025, regulations SI 89/2015 to SI 57/2026), the eight CIU annual reports 2017/18-2024/25 and the 2024-25 budget address. Laws: all fees and minimums recorded as rules. Annual reports: applications received/granted/denied by month, quarter, year, region and country of birth (charts read from text layers, OCR and enlarged crops), revenue, programme-cost and operating-expense lines, NEF collections and remittances by quarter, COVID-19 and National Action Bond purchases with quantities, transfers to government and the NEF, due diligence provider statistics. CIU balance sheets and cash flows are left as a to-do.

events.title: Citizenship by Investment Act assented
events.description: Governor-General assents to the Citizenship by Investment Act No. 14 of 2015 (passed by the House of Assembly 28 July 2015 and the Senate 4 August 2015); the Act carries the date 24 August 2015 in its heading. It creates the CBI Board, the CIU and the Saint Lucia National Economic Fund.
events.quote: PEARLETTE LOUISY, Governor-General. August 17, 2015.

events.title: Citizenship by Investment Regulations made
events.description: SI 89 of 2015 sets four investment options (National Economic Fund US$200,000; approved real estate US$300,000; enterprise US$3.5m or US$6m joint; non-interest bonds US$500,000), the fee schedule, a US$3m financial-resources affidavit and a cap of 500 granted applications a year.
events.quote: The Board may grant up to a maximum of 500 applications for citizenship by investment, annually.

events.title: Amendment regulations SI 105 of 2016 published
events.description: SI 105 of 2016 (made 22 Dec 2016, in force 1 Jan 2017) revokes regulation 7(3) and (7) (including the US$3m financial-resources affidavit), lets the Board keep 20% of each NEF contribution for marketing, adds the US$50,000 bond administration fee and lowers the NEF minimums (US$100,000 alone).
events.quote: Regulation 7 of the principal Regulations is amended by revoking subregulations (3) and (7).

events.title: Admin fee waiver for real estate projects with a school
events.description: New reg. 13A waives the real estate administration fee for applicants and dependants where the approved project includes an educational institution and a child dependant has a letter of acceptance; new reg. 13B waives the processing fee for the COVID-19 bond.
events.quote: A non-refundable administration fee with regard to an approved real estate project that includes an educational institution shall be waived

events.title: COVID-19 relief bond deadline extended to end-2021
events.description: SI 214 of 2020 (made 23 Dec 2020) extends the deadline for purchasing the COVID-19 relief bond to 31 December 2021.
events.quote: “(a) be made by the 31st day of December, 2021;”.

events.title: COVID-19 relief bond deadline extended to end-2022
events.description: SI 4 of 2022 (made 30 Dec 2021) extends the deadline for purchasing the COVID-19 relief bond to 31 December 2022.
events.quote: “(a) be made by the 31st day of December, 2022;”.

events.title: Due diligence fee raised and new application forms
events.description: SI 162 of 2023 raises the applicant due diligence fee to US$8,000, sets administration fees for enterprise Options 1-3 and replaces the application forms (checklist SL1, SL2A/B, SL4 investment confirmation, promoter licence form; the forms state that a name change is not permitted within five years of citizenship).
events.quote: Applicant US$ 8,000”;

events.title: Share of CIU surplus to the Sovereign Wealth Fund
events.description: New s. 19A: between 10% and 25% of the CIU year-end balance, after its operating needs, is to be paid to the Sovereign Wealth Fund of Saint Lucia.
events.quote: No less than ten per cent and no more than twenty-five per cent of any balance at the end of the financial year

events.title: Residency and genuine-link requirements take effect
events.description: New s. 30A requires applicants and dependants to meet prescribed residency and genuine-link requirements from 1 January 2026.
events.quote: Subsection (1) takes effect from the 1st day of January, 2026.

events.title: Name changes barred for five years; OECS denials
events.description: Amendment Act bars new citizens from changing their name within five years of the certificate of registration (with exceptions, and a due diligence check on later changes) and lets the Board deny an applicant already denied by another OECS member state.
events.quote: A citizen shall not change his or her name within five years of being issued a certificate of registration

events.title: Annual cap of 1,500 approvals; 25% NEF marketing retention
events.description: SI 57 of 2026 caps approvals at 1,500 a year (applications received in FY2024-2025 excluded), raises the share of each NEF contribution kept for marketing to 25%, sets a US$350,000 financial-resources affidavit, closes new approvals of real estate projects after 1 Dec 2025, requires biometrics and new due diligence and administration fees.
events.quote: the Board may approve a maximum of one thousand and five hundred applications for citizenship by investment, annually.

events.title: No new real estate project applications after 1 December 2025
events.description: SI 57 of 2026 (published 23 March 2026) inserts reg. 10(10): an application for approval of a real estate project must not be made after 1 December 2025.
events.quote: An application for approval of a real estate project under this regulation must not be made after the 1st day of December, 2025.

events.title: Honey Moon Beach Resort approved as CBI real estate project
events.description: Cabinet Conclusion No. 681 approves the Honey Moon Beach Resort (209 acres at Savannes Bay; two AMResorts properties; gross development cost printed as $343.8M) as an approved real estate project, the first in the 2017/18 report.
events.quote: approved via Cabinet Conclusion number 681 of September 4th,2017.

events.title: Applicants resident in or citizens of Iran no longer accepted
events.description: The CBI Board decided in August 2018 to stop accepting applicants who were residents or citizens of Iran.
events.quote: CIP Saint Lucia decided in August 2018 to stop accepting applicants who were resident/citizens in Iran.

events.description: Chairman reports the first two approved real estate projects (Cannelles development and the Alpina Hotel, part of DSH Pearl of the Caribbean) and the renegotiation of both marketing agent agreements (exclusivities removed, common commission framework) during 2019/20; exact dates not given.

events.title: CIU takes on alien landholding licensing
events.description: Alien Landholding (Licensing) Act No. 1 of 2020 (in effect March 2020) and Regulations No. 70 of 2020 (May 2020) give the CIP Unit the processing of certificates of eligibility and alien landholding licences.
events.quote: The CIP Unit now has the mandate to issue Alien Landholding Licenses

events.title: Applications from Russia, Belarus and Iran suspended
events.description: Saint Lucia suspended receipt of CBI applications from Russia, Belarus and Iran in February 2023, citing inability to conduct due diligence and accept funds.
events.quote: Saint Lucia made the decision in February 2023 to suspend receipt of applications from the above noted countries.

events.title: VIBE initiative launched

events.quote: The launch of the VIBE on 1 January 2023,

events.title: Government to fund roads and housing through the CIP
events.description: Budget address 2024-25: houses to be built under the CIP (Rock Hall earmarked); negotiations with a private developer to fund, in the first instance, $200m of the National Road Development Programme through the CIP infrastructure option, with developers recouping costs through CIP; the Prime Minister says the earlier real estate project (Range Hotel) failed to materialise, costing taxpayers $12 million. Amounts printed with a bare $.
events.quote: the government has entered negotiations with a Private Sector Developer to fund, in the first instance, $200m towards our National Road Development Programme.

new_indicators.name: Number of fund contributions (donations) received
new_indicators.definition: Number of monetary investments (donations) into a government CBI fund received in a period, or budgeted, as printed by the programme unit. A count of contributions, not of people.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-lca1 for the Saint Lucia CIU 2017/18 report (111 donations received vs 200 budgeted).

new_indicators.name: Fund contributions approved but not yet collected
new_indicators.definition: Gross fund contributions (donations) owed by applicants whose citizenship has been approved but which had not been collected at a date, as stated by the programme unit. A stock at a date.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-lca1 for the Saint Lucia CIU 2017/18 report (EC$20,479,500 outstanding at 31 March 2018).

new_indicators.name: Fund contributions held by the CBI unit pending remittance
new_indicators.definition: Fund contributions (donations) collected by the CBI unit but not yet paid over to the government or the national fund at a date (or added to that balance in a period), as stated in the unit's accounts.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-lca1 for the Saint Lucia CIU accounts (NEF money held in trust at year end, 2020-2025).

new_indicators.name: Due diligence reports, orders or interviews handled by a provider
new_indicators.definition: Number of due diligence reports, orders, subjects, requests or interviews that a programme's due diligence provider handled for the programme in a period, as printed by the provider or the unit.
